01.event: Rav Asi left his senile mother and went to Eretz Yisrael, and she followed him.
01.turn: He asked Rabbi Yohanan whether he could leave Israel to greet her and misread the reply as anger.
01.outcome: His mother's coffin arrived, and he said he would not have left had he known.
01.summary: Rav Asi's elderly mother made increasingly impossible requests (jewelry, a husband as handsome as him), so he fled to Eretz Yisrael. When he heard she was following, he asked Rabbi Yohanan if he could leave the land to greet her and got an unclear answer plus a blessing. Rabbi Elazar reassured him it was permission, but on the way he heard her coffin was arriving, and said he would not have gone had he known.

02.actor: Rabbi Yehuda, Sumakhos and Rabbi Yosei
02.event: After Rabbi Meir died, Rabbi Yehuda barred his students, but Sumakhos pushed in and taught a halakha.
02.turn: Rabbi Yehuda grew angry at the ruling, until Rabbi Yosei defended it.
02.outcome: Rabbi Yosei argued the case was relevant after all.
02.summary: After Rabbi Meir died, Rabbi Yehuda told his students to keep Meir's vexatious students out, but Sumakhos pushed in and taught Meir's ruling. Rabbi Yehuda angrily dismissed it as irrelevant, since a woman would not be in the courtyard. Rabbi Yosei, fearing it would be said that Meir died, Yehuda was angry and Yosei was silent, spoke up and showed the case could arise.

03.event: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field and asked Rava about it.
03.turn: Rava asked who relinquished the onions to him.
03.outcome: Rava ruled the onions were stolen, so she was not betrothed; a bundle would differ.
03.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field he worked and came to Rava. Rava asked who had relinquished them to him, meaning the owner had not, so the woman was not betrothed. A full bundle would be different, since he could offer the owner a bundle in return.

04.event: Rav Huna met Rav Hamnuna, praised by Rav Hisda, and saw he wore no head cloth.
04.turn: Hamnuna said it was because he was unmarried.
04.outcome: Rav Huna turned his face away and told him not to see him until he married.
04.summary: Rav Hisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna, who asked to meet him. Seeing he did not cover his head, Rav Huna asked why, and Hamnuna said he was unmarried. Rav Huna turned away and told him not to appear before him until he married.

05.actor: The sons of Rav Huna bar Avin and Rabbi Ami
05.event: They bought a maidservant giving a silver piece as collateral instead of the agreed payment.
05.turn: The price rose and the sellers wanted to cancel.
05.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled there was no valid acquisition.
05.summary: The sons of Rav Huna bar Avin bought a maidservant but, lacking the copper coins, gave a silver piece as collateral. When her price rose, the sellers wanted out and they went to Rabbi Ami. He said there were no perutot and no silver piece, so no acquisition took place.

06.event: A man left seven pearls with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without saying whose they were.
06.turn: The heirs and the depositor disputed ownership before Rabbi Ami.
06.outcome: Rabbi Ami awarded them to the depositor because Meyasha was not wealthy and the man gave a distinguishing mark.
06.summary: A man deposited seven pearls in a sheet at Rabbi Meyasha's house, and Meyasha died without instructions. The family and the depositor came before Rabbi Ami, who ruled the pearls were the claimant's, since Meyasha was not rich and the man identified them by a mark.

07.actor: Rami bar Hama's sister and Rav Avya
07.event: Rami bar Hama's sister, married to Rav Avya, lost her marriage contract and they came to Rav Yosef.
07.turn: Rav Yosef explained a Rabbinic view that a husband may support a wife without a contract; Abaye objected.
07.outcome: Rav Yosef told them to go write her a new one.
07.summary: Rami bar Hama's sister, wife of Rav Avya, lost her marriage contract, and they asked Rav Yosef. He cited a dispute about whether living without a contract is permitted; Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir, and Rav Yosef told them to write a new one.
07.missing: The passage itself is just one sentence; the narrative runs into the context segments.

08.event: Rabbi Elai and Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi stood for Rabbi Shimon bar Abba as he passed.
08.turn: He told them they need not stand.
08.outcome: He gave two reasons: they were ordained and he was not, and the Torah does not stand for its students.
08.summary: Two scholars studying stood up when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed. He told them they were not obliged, because they were ordained scholars and he only an associate, and because those engaged in Torah study need not stand.

09.event: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi tricked the Angel of Death into showing him his place in paradise, took his knife and leapt in.
09.turn: The Angel grabbed his cloak; he swore not to return, and heaven ruled the oath held.
09.outcome: He stayed in paradise, returned the knife by divine command, and Elijah cleared a way for him.
09.summary: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was dying, he got the Angel of Death to show him his place in paradise and to lend his knife, then jumped in. The Angel held his cloak, but he swore he would not come, and since he had never annulled an oath, he stayed. The knife was returned on a divine voice's order, and in paradise he met Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai, who doubted his identity over the rainbow.

12.actor: A half-maidservant half-free woman and her master
12.event: A court forced the master of a half-free woman to free her.
12.outcome: She was made free, so that she could marry.
12.summary: Rav Huna bar Ketina reports an incident in which a woman who was half maidservant, half free, had her master forced to free her. The reason given is that she could not marry and men took liberties with her.
12.missing: Told only as a precedent; the story has no detail or turn.

13.event: Sages wished to buy merchandise from the gentile Dama ben Netina for a large profit, but the key was under his sleeping father's head.
13.turn: He refused to disturb his father.
13.outcome: The next year a red heifer was born in his herd; he asked only for the money he had lost.
13.summary: Dama ben Netina of Ashkelon was offered a huge profit by the Sages for goods, but the key lay under his sleeping father's head, so he would not wake him and lost the sale. The following year a red heifer was born in his herd, and when the Sages came, he asked only for what he had lost honoring his father.

15.event: Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa, dying, asked the Angel of Death for thirty days to review his studies, then asked to see his place.
15.turn: The Angel noted he was no Yehoshua ben Levi; Hanina asked for a Torah scroll and was asked whether he had joined those with ra'atan.
15.outcome: A pillar of fire surrounded him; Rabbi Alexandri persuaded it to leave, and Abaye and Rav Adda bar Mattana then traded remarks.
15.summary: Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa, a friend of the Angel of Death, asked him for thirty days to review his learning. Then he asked to see his place and for the knife, and the angel said he was not like Rabbi Yehoshua, who had joined ra'atan patients. Even so, a pillar of fire separated him at death, and Rabbi Alexandri talked it away in the end, saying 'in your own honor'.

16.actor: The daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon
16.event: The Sages set aside four hundred gold coins for her perfume allowance for one day.
16.turn: She blessed them to do the same for their own daughters.
16.summary: When the Sages set aside four hundred gold coins for the daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon's perfume for a single day, she said they should pledge likewise for their daughters, and they answered Amen.

18.actor: Reish Lakish, his disseminator and Rav Hiyya bar Abba
18.event: After Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child died, Reish Lakish visited with his disseminator and had him speak comfort.
18.turn: The first statement seemed to blame the child's death on sins, and the Gemara explains it as praise.
18.outcome: The disseminator delivered blessings for the mourners, comforters and the people.
18.summary: Reish Lakish waited a day and then visited the bereaved Rav Hiyya bar Abba, and had his disseminator speak in turn. First came a comforting lesson, then a blessing of God, a blessing for the mourners, one for the comforters, and one for all Israel. The Gemara notes the opening line could seem to blame the father, but meant he was important enough to be taken for the generation's sins.

19.event: The Sages reversed which scholar held which view on a child's gift and sent it to Rav Mordekhai.
19.turn: Rav Mordekhai recalled that Rav Ashi had ruled the gift valid.
19.outcome: He sent word to correct the attribution.
19.summary: Abaye asked about a child's gift, and two scholars disagreed. The Sages reversed their opinions and sent the report to Rav Mordekhai, who told them to remind Mar son of Rav Ashi that Rav Ashi himself had said the child's gift was valid in all cases.
19.missing: The Sages' motive for reversing the attributions is not given.

20.actor: A man with a yevama and his brother
20.event: A man had a yevama before him and his brother tried to disqualify her with a bill of divorce.
20.turn: The man offered to share the property; the brother feared he would be cheated like the Pumbedita swindler.
20.outcome: The man offered to let him divide the property from now.
20.summary: A man in Mata Mehasya had to do levirate marriage, and his brother tried to disqualify the yevama with a bill of divorce. The man offered to share the property, but the brother feared being cheated as before, so the man said he could divide it right away.
